thingsToDo.title: Waikōloa Petroglyph Preserve
thingsToDo.description: Waikōloa Petroglyph Preserve is a archaeological site in or near Waikoloa Village, Hawaii. Waikōloa Petroglyph Preserve near Waikoloa contains extensive kiʻi pōhaku, or petroglyph fields, on lava flows in the Kohala region. The preserve documents Native Hawaiian cultural expression and is managed with designated trails and interpretation. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.

thingsToDo.title: Anaehoʻomalu Bay
thingsToDo.description: Anaehoʻomalu Bay is a bay and beach in or near Waikoloa Village, Hawaii. Anaehoʻomalu Bay, commonly called A-Bay, is a sheltered bay and beach area on Hawaiʻi Island's Kohala Coast. The site is known for fishpond remnants, resort shoreline access, and calm-water recreation compared with more exposed coast segments. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

thingsToDo.title: Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site
thingsToDo.description: Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site is a national historic site in or near Waikoloa Village, Hawaii. Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site protects a major late-eighteenth-century temple built under Kamehameha I near Kawaihae. The site interprets political unification history and includes additional archaeological structures in the surrounding dry coastal landscape. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

thingsToDo.title: Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area
thingsToDo.description: Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area is a state recreation area in or near Waikoloa Village, Hawaii. Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area on the Kohala Coast protects one of Hawaiʻi Island's longest white-sand beaches. The park provides managed ocean access, shoreline facilities, and habitat stewardship within a heavily visited coastal recreation zone. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation.

thingsToDo.title: Lapakahi State Historical Park
thingsToDo.description: Lapakahi State Historical Park is a state historical park in or near Waikoloa Village, Hawaii. Lapakahi State Historical Park preserves the remains of a pre-contact Hawaiian fishing settlement on North Kohala's lava shoreline. Archaeological features and interpretive trails document traditional subsistence systems and coastal village structure. The site is regularly referenced in statewide historical, environmental, or cultural documentation. Its present-day access and management context shape how residents and visitors use the area.
